### User Story
As a user, I want to earn chips when I reveal a reward card and choose whether to cash out or continue playing so I can decide how much risk to take.

**Priority:** Must Have

### Tasks & Estimates
- [ ] Detect when a reward card is revealed and add 2 chips to the temporary balance (0.5 hrs)
- [ ] Update the chip counter and display a reward message (0.5 hrs)
- [ ] Display Cash Out and Continue buttons after a reward (0.5 hrs)
- [ ] Implement Cash Out functionality to transfer earned chips to the total balance and end the minigame (1 hr)
- [ ] Implement Continue functionality to start the next round using the remaining deck while preserving temporary chips (0.5 hrs)
- [ ] Reset probability and expected value inputs and require correct calculations before another flip (0.5 hrs)
- [ ] Add navigation back to the lobby after cashing out (0.5 hrs)
- [ ] Write tests for rewards, cashing out, continuing, and chip tracking (1 hr)
- [ ] Run tests, debug failures, and verify functionality (0.5 hrs)

opportunities.title: US-34: Release cash reward to finder
opportunities.description:
### Epic: E8 | Track: Staff | Story Points: 3

**User Story:**
As office staff, I want to record when unclaimed cash is handed to its finder after six months, so the item leaves my held list and the payout is on record.

**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then):**
- Given a held cash item past its reward date, when I confirm the finder's identity and record the payout, then the item is marked as paid to the finder, separately from "released to owner", along with who received it, the ID they showed, the staff member and the time.
- Given a cash item whose reward date hasn't arrived, when I try to record a finder payout, then it is refused.
- Given the payout is recorded, then the item drops out of the staff reminders and the held-items list, and stays out of public search.
- Given another office holds the item, when I try to record the payout, then it is refused.

opportunities.title: Intake creates item entries for coins, cash-equivalent treasure and cash quest rewards
opportunities.description:
## Problem
Session 6 Delta Review proposed a NEW `inventory_and_loot` item for every stated amount in one treasure hoard: "New Item — 1,400 cp", "— 1,300 sp", "— 70 gp", "— Art and Gems (9…)". Campaign Manager is not an inventory system: only distinct things of significance become items.

## Cause
- `NARRATIVE_EXTRACT_SYSTEM` rule 6 in `shared/chronicle-ai.js` tells the AI to include coins and to use "one entry per denomination", with `"1400 cp"` as its example.
- The mixed-page schema in `fillRoundsFromText()` describes items as `"<item or coin name>"`.
- `_processNarrativeResult()` in `admin/delta-review.html` turns every `result.items` entry into a NEW item.
- The redesign pipeline has the same gap: the step 2 "thing" definition in `shared/chronicle-entities.js` is "a notable object or treasure", and step 4 loot facts in `shared/chronicle-facts.js` have no rule.
- `docs/intake-redesign.md` lists "coins found" as an example of a Thing.

## Rule
- **Cash or cash equivalent, never an item:** coins, currency, payments, and any gem, art object or treasure with a stated cash value ("emerald worth 100 GP", "2 smoky quartz, 25 GP each", "art and gems").
  - **As a quest reward:** a narrative note on the quest, written as the notes state it ("Rewarded 200 GP and an emerald worth 30 GP"), with `reward_received.value_gp` set to the total stated value (230). No item entry, no `item_refs`.
  - **Found any other way:** narrative in the session (`session_notes` / passages).
- **Possible item:** a gem or object described by something other than its price, with no value given ("oddly warm gem", "shimmering diamond"). Proposed for the DM to confirm.
- **Always an item:** named or magic items (Immovable Rod, +1 Moon Sickle) and quest objects (maps, letters, keys).

## Approach
- Rewrite rule 6 and the mixed-page items schema to the rule above; route treasure into `session_notes` and quest rewards into the quest.
- Apply the same rule to step 2 "thing" mentions and step 4 loot facts.
- Client-side guard in `_processNarrativeResult()` that drops currency-only or priced-pile names the AI still returns, and adds them to the page summary as narrative so nothing is lost.
- Fix the "coins found" example in `docs/intake-redesign.md`.
- Tests: guard cases (cp/sp/gp amounts, "Art and Gems (…)", priced gems) vs kept items (Silver Dagger, Golden Idol, Potion of Healing ×2, oddly warm gem); prompt text for all four paths.

## Done when
- Re-interpreting the session 6 hoard page proposes no coin, priced-gem or pile items, and the treasure appears as narrative.
- A quest page with a cash reward adds a narrative note and `value_gp` on the quest, and no item.
- Named items and unpriced distinctive objects still come through.

## Related data cleanup (done directly, not by this issue)
- Remove `item_009` "Trade Commission" and its refs (session_004 `items_found`, qst_004 `reward_received.item_refs`).
- Remove `item_010` "Unrefined Emerald" and its refs (session_005 `items_found` and `key_moments[1].ref`, qst_005 `reward_received.item_refs`). Item says Helen paid it, qst_005 says Krustie Gnome — confirm which before removing.

opportunities.title: Competitions: award cash, reputation and honours exactly once
opportunities.description:
Part of #323. Source: [Career progression, competitions and rewards](https://app.notion.com/p/4150870d4c44810c880ae3395086e9d0?pvs=204), CPP-07; CPP-06 payout outcomes.

**Delivery outcome:** A.

**Prerequisites:** #570, #571, #559

## Work

- Implement saved reward identities and one atomic award path for competition cash, reputation, honours and future entitlement records.
- Connect the Open Cup's published progression prizes and neutral/home income rules to FIN-04; distinguish ordinary fixture cash from extra round prizes and never pay a bye.
- Store honours with season, competition, club and winning squad. Definition snapshots preserve promised rewards if catalogue data changes later.
- Persist reward state through result replay, report reopening, save/load, held-match recovery and rollover. Leave earned cap calculation to the cap integration issue.

**Done when:** Cash/reputation/honours reconcile with recorded outcomes and the published prize table, every award is applied once, and duplicate completion/reload/report opening cannot grant another reward or alter an existing trophy.

## Validation

Award idempotency, normal and cancelled fixtures, no-bye rewards, neutral income splitting, cap-entitlement records with no premature activation and failure with no partial application.

## Likely code areas

Existing finance/money and result ownership operations; state reward/honour records and season statistics/history.

## Delivery

Follow current AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, state ownership and save-recovery contracts. One focused change per PR (split the ticket if implementation reveals separate deliverables); required TypeScript/Vitest/build, CI/QA and an independent checker for implementation. Update repository hub and the Notion spec when behaviour lands. Keep .github workflows, Android manual dispatch, monetisation and unrelated match-rule changes outside this ticket. Coordinate shared state/save/time files sequentially with the finance and progression work. Issue creation records planned work, not implementation, test evidence or merge permission.

opportunities.title: Present non-cash reward rows and Present-added sound in stage-won ledger
opportunities.description:
Depends on #648 documentation and mixed reward foundation #649. Canonical design: doc/presents.md, especially Mixed reward ledger and sound; lifecycle context: doc/game-events.md.

Present registered non-cash reward entries alongside cash rows. Stage-three reward includes one **Present added** row after existing cash rows, with no change to the displayed cash sum. Each registered entry presentation handler supplies its display value and configured SFX; no Present/source/kind switch in generic menus. The row reveals in the normal ledger sequence, and the next action appears after every row finishes. Reuse current result-menu work #531 rather than a parallel menu.

Register reward.present with an appropriate placeholder and family/description; play it when the row is revealed and refresh sfx:usage. It must not unwrap or reveal payload, create cards, advance RNG or pay again. Preserve coin row sounds/totals. Include screenshots or a recording and review URL showing stage-one/two cash ledgers and stage-three mixed ledger; verify Continue, re-entry and cancellation with no repeated model awards. Run required checks. Production synth/sample content can follow independently.


## Design reference and gate

Canonical contract: [presents.md#mixed-reward-ledger-and-sound](https://github.com/trebizondoculpepper/poker_blocks/blob/main/doc/presents.md#mixed-reward-ledger-and-sound). Documentation prerequisite: #648. If that documentation ticket is still open, wait for its merge; a link to an unmerged design is not implementation approval. Follow the native prerequisites for shared implementation work too. This current contract supersedes earlier conflicting provisional/historical notes; no new owner decision is required for its documented defaults.

## Mission (revenue-first)
Turn the deployed founding beta into a revenue-producing rewards platform. Do not substitute XP for cash or fabricated partner inventory.

**Verified release:** Railway `earnloop-web` from `Noetfield-Systems/Earnloop@a8f4dc502649f48a931c34845d6cdf9379f1bb08` with retained PostgreSQL and public domain https://earnloop-web-production.up.railway.app/. Independent HTTP smoke **PASS**: https://github.com/Noetfield-Systems/Earnloop/actions/runs/42756970996. Current members=0, early access=0, partner funding unverified.

### Acceptance gates
- [ ] Publisher account approved by Torox / ayeT / equivalent, with genuine available Canadian inventory and signed contract (Founder/operator approval required)
- [ ] Implement exact partner authenticated postback spec, unique conversion IDs, replay protection, tracking, reversal and dispute handling; never trust client-reported spend
- [ ] Real booked advertiser payable and independently verified cash settlement with evidence
- [ ] Reward ledger records funded user liability separately from community XP, and supports reversal/chargebacks
- [ ] Legal/payment provider integration, identity recovery, user eligibility, KYC where applicable and permitted cash-out/gift-card fulfilment
- [ ] First real, consented user completes partner action and receives real funded reward; attach partner statement, payout receipt, IDs, timestamp, independent verification and contribution margin
- [ ] Company OS captures verified evidence, net contribution and next acquisition action in product WorkPackets; Sina Founder OS gets portfolio summary only

**Do not claim launch revenue until funds are actually settled. No paid offers/cashouts are activated without approved partners and funded settlement.**

opportunities.title: Offer a cash-payment discount at the till
opportunities.description:
## Why
Where the law allows it, a restaurant may reward cash payments. This is the other side of #264 (card surcharge). US-only; hidden where not permitted.

## What it does
- A location setting for a cash discount percentage.
- Applied at the till when the cashier takes cash, shown as its own line.
- Reported separately.

## Rules and edge cases
- Hidden in regions where it is not allowed.
- Never stacks with a card surcharge on the same order.

## Where we are today
Nothing found for a cash discount.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Taking cash applies the configured percentage and prints a separate line.
- [ ] Reports show cash discounts as their own figure.
- [ ] The setting is not shown for KSA organizations.

opportunities.title: Reward system
opportunities.description:
Act as an expert full-stack developer and UI/UX designer. I am building a mobile-first web app (HTML/Tailwind CSS/JS) for 14-year-old boys to track household chores using a gaming-inspired theme (Valorant, Minecraft, Roblox aesthetic). 

Implement a Loss-Aversion Point Engine and Reward System using the following architecture:

1. DUAL-CURRENCY SYSTEM:
- XP (Experience Points): Earned ONLY through task completion. Permanent, cumulative, and never lost or docked. Drives overall level and gamer ranks (Unranked -> Iron -> Bronze -> Silver -> Gold -> Platinum -> Diamond -> Ascendant -> Radiant).
- Coins: Earnable spending currency used in the Rewards Shop.

2. LOSS-AVERSION & PENALTY MECHANICS:
- Missed / Failed Daily Tasks: Deduct Coins from the available balance (or forfeit the daily Coin multiplier) to leverage psychological loss aversion without touching permanent XP.
- Guardrail: Implement a minimum Coin threshold (e.g., balance cannot drop below zero) and clear penalty limits per task so kids don't feel a "sunk-cost demotivation" trap.
- Streak System: Track consecutive active days (🔥 Streak). Missing mandatory daily tasks resets or reduces the streak bonus multiplier.

3. REWARDS SHOP LIST (Structured Tiers):
Implement a customizable Rewards Shop with the following pre-loaded catalog:
- Tier 1 (Micro / Low Cost):
  * +30 Min Gaming Extension
  * One-Time Minor Chore Pass (Skip a task)
  * +30 Min Weekend Bedtime Buffer
- Tier 2 (Mid-Tier / Moderate Cost):
  * Choose Friday Night Dinner / Takeout
  * In-Game Currency / Cosmetic Allowance (Robux, V-Bucks, Valorant Points)
  * Uninterrupted Gaming Session / Sleepover with Friends
- Tier 3 (Boss-Level / High Cost):
  * Gaming Gear Upgrade (Headset, Mouse, Keyboard Cap)
  * Funded Outing with Friends (Movies, Arcade, Bowling)
  * Cash-Out Point Conversion

4. PARENT CONTROL OVERRIDES:
- PIN-protected parent mode to approve completed high-value tasks, issue direct bonus/penalty Coin adjustments, and process reward redemptions.

Please generate or update the application code to fully integrate this logic, store state in local storage, and present a sleek, high-contrast dark mode UI optimized for smartphone web browsers.

opportunities.description:
## Goal

A creator, and Genfeed itself, runs a full newsletter from app.genfeed.ai: write or generate an issue, send it to subscribers in the brand's own look, see who opened and clicked, and charge for it in GEN credits. One module, one place in the app, no outside newsletter tool.

Document only. The week of 11-09 is a coding lock; nothing here starts until Vincent gives the go.

## Today (verified in code at master `e39a197c`)

- Authoring exists: `Newsletter` model with generation, approval, schedule (`packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma`), API at `collections/newsletters`, editor under `apps/web/app/(protected)/[orgSlug]/[brandSlug]/edit/newsletter`.
- Delivery today is only to a connected third-party publication (`long-form-deliveries.service.ts`). Genfeed never emails an issue itself.
- `renderNewsletterHtml` turns Markdown into sanitized HTML. There is **no email layout**: no brand logo, banner, colors, footer or plain-text part.
- Resend sends our own mail one message at a time (`apps/server/notifications/src/services/resend/resend.service.ts`). No batch, no audience.
- Delivery analytics exist for system mail: `EmailMessage` (accepted, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained), first-party `EmailClick`, signed Resend webhook, suppression list (`email-performance.service.ts`). They are tied to a registered `userId`, so they cannot yet cover outside subscribers.
- No subscriber model, no subscribe endpoint, no CSV import. The marketing footer's newsletter block links to a third-party sign-up page.
- Brand has colors, font, watermark logo ids and an end card; `BANNER` exists as an asset category (`asset.enum.ts`). No dedicated newsletter header fields.

## Recommendation

Yes, make it a module. The pieces share one subscriber table, one send pipeline and one analytics store, and splitting them across the article, profile and credits work would duplicate all three. The module is one app section (Issues, Subscribers, Analytics, Settings) over three API modules: subscribers, sends, analytics.

## Scope and existing issues

| Area | Issue |
| --- | --- |
| Creator profile URLs and showcase | #9662, #9661 (under #9666) |
| Public subscribe, subscriber model, double opt-in, first send | #9665 (under #9666) |
| Credits ledger, tips, paid subscriptions, paid issues, earnings, cash-out decision | #9715 to #9720 (under #9714) |
| App section and module boundaries | new, linked below |
| Subscriber management: add by email, CSV import and export | new |
| Email template and brand identity | new |
| Bulk delivery engine | new (carves the engine out of #9665) |
| Tracking and analytics | new |
| Genfeed's own newsletter: homepage, footer, archive | new |
| Remove third-party newsletter platform references | new |

## Order

1. Decisions below.
2. #9662 URLs, then subscriber model and subscribe flow (#9665 first half).
3. Subscriber management in the app (add, CSV).
4. Email template and brand identity.
5. Bulk delivery engine, then tracking and analytics.
6. Genfeed's own newsletter on the homepage, then the reference cleanup (needs a working sign-up before the old link goes).
7. Credits: #9715, #9716, #9717, #9718, #9719. #9720 is a decision, not a build.

## Decisions needed before building

- Sending domain: shared Genfeed domain first, or each brand verifies its own.
- Plan limits: subscribers and sends per month per plan (Cloud runtime gate).
- Platform fee on paid issues (from #9714).
- Whether the existing connected-publication delivery stays as an optional target.
- Whether CSV import needs a per-import consent confirmation (recommended: yes).

## Done when

A visitor subscribes on Genfeed's homepage, confirms by email, and receives the next issue in Genfeed's look; the owner imports a CSV in the app; the issue shows opens and clicks; a paid issue is unlocked with credits. Each sub-issue has its own finish condition and evidence.

opportunities.title: Epic: Creator earnings in GEN credits (tips, paid subscriptions, paid articles)
opportunities.description:
## Goal

Readers can pay creators in GEN credits, and creators spend what they earn on generation inside Genfeed. This completes the creator publishing loop started in #9666: write, publish, email subscribers (#9665), get paid.

Document only. The week of 11-09 is a coding lock, so no code is scheduled.

## Today (verified in code at master `e0d9b108`)

- `CreditBalance` and `CreditTransaction` belong to an organization or billing account, never to a user (`packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma`).
- Transaction categories are `add`, `deduct`, `expire`, `reset`, `rollover`, `refund`, `byok-usage` (`packages/contracts/src/enums/credit.enum.ts`). There is **no transfer between accounts**, no tip, no paid subscription to a creator.
- Stripe is used only for Genfeed's own plans (`Subscription`, `UserSubscription`). No Stripe Connect and no payout code.
- `Article` and `Newsletter` have no price or access fields. Every published article is public.

## Scope

Earn-and-spend only: earned credits are spent on generation inside Genfeed and are not withdrawable. This avoids payouts, KYC and tax handling. Cash-out is a separate decision (see the last issue).

## Order

1. Credit transfer ledger (everything else builds on it).
2. Tips.
3. Paid subscriptions to a creator.
4. Paid articles and newsletter issues.
5. Creator earnings view.
6. Decision: cash-out.

## Decisions needed before building

- Platform fee on each payment (percentage, or none at first).
- Whether earned credits expire like purchased ones, or never expire.
- Whether earned credits count toward plan limits and the low-credits banner.
- Who can pay: signed-in Genfeed users only, or a guest checkout that creates an account.

## Done when

A reader with credits tips a creator, subscribes to them, and unlocks a paid article. The creator's balance rises by the amount minus the fee, and the creator spends it on a generation. Each sub-issue carries its own finish condition and evidence.

opportunities.title: Issue invoices for paid sessions and bundles
opportunities.description:
Clients have no invoice or receipt for what they pay, while the seeded marketing copy says "EU-compliant invoices provided".

**Current state**
- `web/src/` contains no invoice code.
- Checkout sessions are created in `web/src/app/actions/booking.ts` and in `createStripeCheckout` (`web/src/app/actions/stripe.ts`), without `invoice_creation`.
- `web/supabase/migrations/00028_seed_homepage_sections.sql` and `00030_neutral_branding.sql` contain the "Invoice provided" claim.
- `web/src/app/(client)/my-sessions/[id]/page.tsx` shows the amount only.

**Scope**
- Enable Stripe Checkout invoice creation on both checkout paths, with the therapist's name and the line-item description.
- Store the invoice id and hosted URL on `payments` from the `checkout.session.completed` webhook (new migration).
- Add a "Download invoice" link on the client session page and on therapist earnings rows.
- Show the refund state next to the invoice when a payment is refunded.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A paid single session and a paid bundle each produce an invoice
- [ ] The invoice link is visible only to that client and that therapist
- [ ] Free and credit-paid sessions show no invoice link
- [ ] Webhook test covers storing the invoice reference

opportunities.title: feat(verification): pilot Paid-managed verification of Paid user journeys
opportunities.description:
## Problem

Paid can provision a browser sidecar and Playwright MCP for an issue implementation run, derive a start command, and record interactive verification. The agent still has to rediscover how to exercise each Paid feature. Paid's own `.paid/screenshots.yml` already defines auth, seed data, and routes, but it is oriented toward screenshot capture rather than repeatable changed-feature journeys.

## Goal

Use Paid to verify changes to Paid itself. In an isolated development/test run where the Paid repository is the managed project, a Paid `create_pr` agent should be able to start a seeded Paid instance, sign in, exercise a relevant Paid user journey, inspect the observed result, and attach that evidence to its existing run result.

## Scope

- Pilot one representative Paid web journey first (for example, sign-in → Projects → project detail), then exercise a real changed feature through a Paid-managed implementation run.
- Add a repository-owned, concise journey guide and only the helper commands needed to make setup, data reset, navigation, observation, and cleanup repeatable. Reuse `.paid/screenshots.yml` for existing routes/auth/seed configuration; do not create a competing copy.
- Teach `AgentRuns::VerificationPrompt` to discover the guide at a conventional path and select the journey relevant to the changed surface. Reuse the existing Playwright MCP sidecar, runtime plan, app diagnostics, and `VerificationResultRecorder`.
- Keep all test data and application execution in the isolated run environment. No production Paid data or credentials.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can follow the documented commands from a clean Paid checkout to start a seeded Paid instance, obtain a test identity, complete the selected journey through Playwright MCP, inspect the expected result, and clean up resources created by the run.
- [ ] A Paid-managed `create_pr` run against the Paid repository performs the journey for a real changed feature and stores the actual steps, observed result, relevant log/trace/screenshot references, and reviewed commit in the existing verification result. A screenshot or agent claim alone is not treated as proof of the criterion.
- [ ] The journey and its commands have a focused, executable maintenance check so a stale route, login step, or startup instruction fails visibly.
- [ ] Missing setup, authentication failure, unavailable browser, or failed assertion yields explicit failed/skipped/not-run evidence; it cannot be reported as a successful journey.
- [ ] The pilot reports setup time, run time, failure modes, and operator effort before proposing wider rollout.

## Boundaries and related work

`bootstrap_readiness` has a narrow write allowlist. Journey guides or behavior-bearing helper scripts must use a normal reviewed PR or a separately designed write boundary; this issue does not widen bootstrap authority. Preserve current project verification opt-in and merge policy. Follow Full LID through the owning HLD/LLD/EARS, failing-first tests, and code.

Relevant foundations: `docs/intent/live-web-app-preview/`, `docs/intent/project-readiness/`, `app/services/agent_runs/verification_prompt.rb`, and `.paid/screenshots.yml`.

Inspired by Lauren Tan's [verification-skill article](https://x.com/poteto/article/2094457600259842065).

opportunities.title: Fully paid draft invoices should remain drafts (paid != completed)
opportunities.description:
### Issue filing prerequisites

- [x] I've checked the [documentation](https://docs.invoiceshelf.com/).
- [x] I've looked for similar issues both Open and Closed.
- [x] I've tried clearing both cache and cookies in my browser or tried opening the app in the Incognito/InPrivate window.

### Describe the bug

Recording a payment that fully covers a draft invoice changes its status from DRAFT to COMPLETED, although the invoice has never been sent. It is no longer identifiable as a draft, and the completed status suggests that the invoice is finalized and, depending on the editing settings, no longer editable. There is no longer a draft status to indicate that work such as sending the invoice is still pending.

Reducing or deleting that payment can then change the same invoice back to DRAFT and make it editable again, depending on the configured editing restrictions. A payment correction can therefore reopen an invoice that appeared to be finalized, without any explicit action to reopen it.

### Steps to Reproduce the issue

1. Set retrospective edits to be disabled after sending an invoice.
2. Create a draft invoice with a positive total and leave it unsent.
3. Record a payment covering the full invoice amount.
4. Open the invoice and check its status and edit permission.
5. Reduce or delete the payment, then check the invoice status and edit permission again.

### Expected behaviour

The invoice remains DRAFT, its paid_status becomes PAID, and the recorded payment remains associated with it. Its draft status continues to indicate that it has not yet been sent. Later payment corrections update the payment status without implicitly finalizing or reopening the draft.

Editing follows the configured retrospective edit setting: a restriction based on sending should not lock an unsent draft, while payment-based restrictions should still apply.

### Actual behaviour

The invoice becomes COMPLETED solely because it was fully paid. With editing disabled after sending, it can no longer be edited despite never having been sent. Its status hides the fact that it is still an unsent draft and gives the impression that no further action is needed.

Reducing or deleting the payment changes it back to DRAFT; with the same setting, it becomes editable again.

### Docker

- [x] App running in Docker Container.
- [x] Docker container running behind Reverse proxy.

2.4.7
